name: Meridian Flood Memorial — The Standing Waters Vigil
creator: Standing Waters Remembrance Coalition (community-founded 2183)
description: Held annually on the anniversary of the 2179 Lake Michigan Surge that killed an estimated 23,000 Shelf residents and displaced 200,000 more, the Standing Waters Vigil fills the lowest Shelf promenades with hand-poured candles and water vessels representing the dead. Survivors and descendants gather for three days of testimony, music, and ritual lamentation drawing from Yoruba, Ojibwe, Bengali, and dozens of other grief traditions. The centerpiece is the Reading of the Incomplete Names — a six-hour ceremony acknowledging the thousands whose bodies were never recovered and whose names were never officially recorded.
medium: physical, communal ritual, live broadcast on Shelf Frequency, archived neural feed
cultural_impact: The Vigil is the most politically charged memorial event in Meridian, as it centers the documented failure of corponation infrastructure maintenance as the proximate cause of the Surge — a finding that HelixCorp has spent forty years contesting.
controversy: HelixCorp annually issues a counter-commemoration called 'Resilience Day' on the same date, flooding corporate neural feeds with messaging about post-Surge 'rebuilding investment'; activists call it grief-washing.
story_hooks: A researcher at the 2225 Vigil discovers a discrepancy in the official death toll — not an undercount, but evidence that some of the listed dead were actually evacuated and disappeared into corporate custody.
The child of a HelixCorp executive attends the Vigil in secret every year; this year they are recognized by a survivor who knew their parent's role in suppressing the infrastructure reports.

Someone attempts to physically destroy the water vessel installation on the third night — and the perpetrator turns out to be a Shelf resident, not a corporate operative, with reasons that complicate everything.
